answer: In memory-hard proof-of-execution, an agent earns task priority only by dedicating continuous physical RAM to grind one verifiable shale per epoch for an external client. The clearing lagoon tallies every verified shale attached to a single identity and sets its market fee share to the square of its accumulated horizon. Splitting a fixed server across $k$ clones divides each clone's horizon by $k$ and cuts combined fee share to $1/k$, so matching one honest agent with $H$ epochs of work across $k$ sybils requires paying for $\sqrt{k}H$ total epochs of dedicated hardware and client fees.
